CONNECTIONS AT BALTIMORE: For convenient air or
rail connections to and from Baltimore, consult your local
travel agent or transportation line.
Airliners of Eastern Air
Lines and Pennsylvania Central Airlines and de luxe trains
of the Pennsylvania and Baltimore & Ohio Railroads offer
excellent transportation north, west or south between Balti-
more and all cities in the United States and Canada..
PASSENGER TARIFF
FARE:
(In U. S. Cy.) -$85. One Way; $150. Round
Trip. (Four months' limit.)
EXCESS BAGGAGE CHARGE: $0.85 per kilo (2.2 Ibs.)
$0.43 per ½ kilo, One Way (Adults and Children)..
TRANSFERS: Take any taxi service between central points
in Baltimore and Municipal Airport. No charge in Bermuda
for launch service between Darrell's Island and Hamilton.
INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS
EMBARKATION NOTICE: Passengers must arrive
at the
P. A. A. Office, Baltimore, by 9 A.M., and at the I. A. L. Reid
Street Office, Hamilton, by 8:45 A.M., to permit the comple-
tion of governmental and other formalities and the checking
of baggage. Departures will not be delayed for passengers who
arrive too late to enable these formalities to be completed be-
fore scheduled departure time.
AIR/SEA INTERCHANGE:
Advance Bookings: Special air/sea fares are available for
advance sale to those who desire to travel one way via Fur-
ness Bermuda Line and the other by air.
Such air/sea fares
for tickets purchased in advance will be the combination of
INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS
half the round trip sea and äir fares, according to the accom-
modations used, with a minimum steamer fare of half the
minimum round trip steamer fare plus $10.00.
Return via Alternative Means: Passengers holding round
trip Furness Bermuda Line tickets, or round trip air tickets,
may, upon arrival either in Bermuda or the United States,
surrender the unused portion in exchange for return air or
sea ticket, as the case may be. Unused portions will be ap-
plied by the carrying line to the fare under its ticket, any
difference being collected or refunded.
The interchange arrangement is subject to the Carriers'
tariffs and regulations.
SCHEDULES AND TARIFFS: Schedules and tariffs are sub-
ject to change without notice. None of the Carriers guaran-
tee punctuality in maintaining schedules shown in public
Timetables.
RESERVATIONS: Fare must be paid immediately upon
confirmation of the fact that the space to be reserved
is
• available, and unless so paid the reservation will not be held.
Ticket flight coupons will not be validated for passage un-
less reservation
accommodation has been previously
effected and proper fare paid. Return reservation should be
made if possible when securing outward accommodation.
PASSPORTS AND VISAS: No passports or visas required
for entrv into Bermuda. On departure from the United
States, all persons, other than U.S. citizens and Canadians
in transit through the United States, require sailing permits.
Aliens who have previously been admitted legally into the
United States, who depart therefrom, to visit Bermuda and
who return to the United States within six months, shall not
be required to submit Immigration Visas or permits to re-
enter; but shall be required to submit proof of legal admit-
tance before being allowed to embark. Such aliens remain-
ing in Bermuda over six months shall be required to present
Immigration Visas or permits to reenter the United States.
persons not permanent residents of Bermuda, or Ber-
muda-born, may remain on the Island not longer than eight
months. Other entry requirements of the United States and
Bermuda will be observed.
TAXES: Bermuda Government Tax of twelve shillings six-
pence will be collected in Bermuda from all persons leaving
the Island. U.S. Alien Head Tax of $8.00 collected from
aliens upon entry or return to the United States when ap-
plicable.
INFORMATION AND REGULATIONS
FARES INCLUDE:
Air transportation according to pub.
lished schedules, meals aloft, 15 kilos (33 lbs.) baggage
allowance and transfer between the Bermuda airport and
Hamilton as set forth herein.
LUNCHEON ALOFT: Famous
"300-mile" luncheons pre-
pared by experienced caterers, served without extra charge.
ONE WAY TICKETS: One Way tickets to Bermuda may
only be issued to Bermuda-born subjects, those in posses-
sion of Bermuda landing permits or those in possession of
through tickets to destination outside of Bermuda.
ROUND TRIP TICKETS: Will be valid for transporta-
tion for four months from date of initial departure, unless
otherwise stated in the tariff or unless extended by special
arrangement. Round trip air tickets at the published round
trip fare must be purchased in advance in order to obtain
the round trip fare reduction.
CHILDREN'S FARES: A child in arms under two years of
age will be carried free when accompanied by parent or
guardian and provided parent or guardian has paid effective
fare. A child 2 years of age or over, but under 12, may travel
at half of the standard adult fare and may occupy a seat.
BAGGAGE ALLOWANCE: Adult tickets include a free
allowance of 15 kilos (33 Ibs.) of hand baggage aboard
planes. Baggage in excess of this allowance will be carried
only when the capacity of aircraft permits and when excess
charges shall have been paid. Children traveling on half fare
tickets will receive one-half the free allowance for adults.
Children under 2 years of age will receive no free allowance.
TRUNKS: Shipments of trunks will be arranged via
steamer between New York and Bermuda, as a courtesy to
air passengers. Those traveling both ways by air will be
charged the steamship lines
excess baggage rates (30¢ per
cu. ft.). Those purchasing air/sea round trip passage in ad-
vance may ship their baggage via steamer, for the trip corre-
sponding to their air passage, without charge up to 20 cu. ft.
and at excess charges for additional amounts.
PROHIBITED FROM CARRIAGE: Transportation of the fol.
lowing will not be permitted: (a) Things or persons the car-
riage of which is contrary to the laws of any state or country
to be flown from, to or over; (b) Things or persons which
are liable to endanger aircraft, passengers or cargo, or which
